items.title: Send these readings to your care team today
items.text: Your blood sugar readings were higher than the target, so contact your care team today to discuss what you can do. Your average reading was 198.1 mg/dL, and 9.9% of your readings were above 250 mg/dL.

items.title: Try a 10 to 20 minute walk after dinner
items.text: You walked after 0 of your scored meals, too few to measure your own effect yet. Across the program, a walk after dinner went with a rise about 18.3 mg/dL smaller in the same person, more than after other meals (14.6 mg/dL). 10 to 19 minutes got most of the gain: 17.5 mg/dL less, against 19.5 for 20-29 minutes and 16.6 for 30+ minutes. A check in real adults (CGMacros) pointed the same way, at about a fifth of the program's size, but it is not proven there yet.

rejected.text: Walking after dinner may help with your blood sugar, as it went with a rise about 18.3 mg/dL smaller in the same person. Walking for 10 to 19 minutes got most of the gain, with a rise of 17.5 mg/dL less.

items.title: Move dinner earlier
items.text: Having dinner late, at 8 pm or later, went with sugar rising about 9.2 mg/dL more after late dinners than after earlier ones. Try to start dinner before 8 pm to see if it makes a difference for you.

items.title: Aim for a 13-hour overnight break
items.text: You averaged 11.2 hours of overnight fasting, which is something to discuss with your care team. In a study, adding overnight fasting to coaching changed HbA1c by -0.03 points compared with coaching alone.
